title: Give as You Have Been Blessed

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Count off seven weeks from the time you begin to put the sickle to the standing grain. Then celebrate the Festival of Weeks to the Lord your God by giving a freewill offering in proportion to the blessings the Lord your God has given you. - Deut 16:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The second great feast was the Festival of Weeks, held seven weeks after the harvest began. At its heart was a freewill offering given "in proportion to the blessings the Lord your God has given you." Giving here was not a fixed tax squeezed out grudgingly. It was a glad response measured by how much God had already given.

Notice the order. God blesses first, then His people respond with grateful giving. Our generosity is always an answer to His prior kindness, never a way of earning His favour. We give because we have received, not so that we might receive.

This freeing truth carries straight into the New Testament, where Paul says God loves a cheerful giver and urges us to give as we have decided in our hearts, not reluctantly or under compulsion (2 Cor 9:7). When we grasp how richly God has blessed us, most of all in the gift of His Son, our hands loosen naturally. Giving stops feeling like loss and starts feeling like worship. Look honestly at what God has entrusted to you. A generous heart is not about the size of the gift but the gratitude behind it. How is God's blessing shaping the way you give?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you give out of gratitude or out of obligation?
2. How has God blessed you in ways you often overlook?
3. What would cheerful, proportionate giving look like for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for blessing me first, most of all in Jesus. Make me a cheerful, grateful giver with open hands. Amen.
